strategies.summary: After a higher-timeframe boundary is tapped, define the retracement context and use OTE only as guidance. Enter on the first overlapping bullish PD array encountered on the pullback, then keep the stop beyond the intermediate-term low instead of tight under the entry.

timeframes.notes: Examples use 1h context with 1m or 5m execution; Daily context is also mentioned. Equilibrium and OTE frame the pullback but are guidelines, not hard entry thresholds.

custom_signals.name: htf_pd_array_tap
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades into a higher-timeframe discount array (bullish) or premium array (bearish), such as a fair value gap or order block.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (low <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled@bias_tf) OR (low <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated@bias_tf)

custom_signals.name: overlapping_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: A fair value gap that shares price with another PD array (order block) on the same timeframe; the shared range is the entry zone.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: max(bullish_fvg[0].gap_low, bullish_ob[0].zone_low) <= min(bullish_fvg[0].gap_high, bullish_ob[0].zone_high) AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated

custom_signals.name: intermediate_term_high
custom_signals.plain_definition: A swing high flanked by a lower swing high on its left and a lower swing high on its right.

custom_signals.name: intermediate_term_low
custom_signals.plain_definition: A swing low flanked by a higher swing low on its left and a higher swing low on its right.

sequence: Wait for price to tap the higher-timeframe boundary that points toward the opposing array.
On the execution chart, enter on the first overlapping bullish PD array encountered on the retracement instead of waiting strictly for OTE.

invalidation.text: Price breaks and sustains beyond the intermediate term low (the origin of the dealing range).

filters.text: Do not go into the 1-minute timeframe without a higher timeframe boundary or context. Doing so creates a reason to trade everywhere, lowering probability.

entry_rule.text: Enter on the first place where a fair value gap overlaps with another discount/premium array (like a breaker or order block).
entry_rule.quote: enter on the first place where we have overlapping PD arrays

target_rule.text: The first target is the immediate intermediate term high. The final target is the ultimate higher timeframe draw on liquidity.
target_rule.quote: first Target being this High second target being that high right there

stop_rule.text: Place the stop loss below the intermediate term low (the start of the dealing range), covering the bodies of the candles. Do not place it tightly just under the entry PD array.
stop_rule.quote: putting it at the intermediate term low right there covering the bodies of the candles

presenter_claims.claim: The strongest magnet before we expand further is the overlapping PD spot.

strategies.notes: The higher-timeframe boundary is the prerequisite for dropping to the execution chart; without it the presenter considers lower-timeframe overlaps low probability. The machine target rule captures the first stated target (the immediate intermediate-term high); the later higher-timeframe draw on liquidity stays in text because structured rules allow one target reference. The canonical overlap proxy is the registry's FVG-plus-order-block confluence, so breaker or mitigation-block examples remain descriptive rather than fully zoned.

signals_observed.bias_source: 1H rejection from a Daily fair value gap heading towards a daily premium array / high.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Higher timeframe establishes context: price bounced from a Daily discount array (FVG) and is heading toward a Daily high.
1-hour dealing range is defined; a 1H overlapping PD array (breaker + FVG) is identified near equilibrium.
Drops to 1-minute timeframe within the 1-hour context area.
First 1-minute entry forms: a breaker overlapping with a fair value gap.
Price expands higher, providing a second entry on a mitigation block overlapping with a fair value gap.
Price reaches the intermediate term high target. This major liquidity sweep causes a deeper retracement into a 15-minute FVG + order block before continuing.

examples.presenter_commentary: He emphasizes that context is the absolute most important part. Without the 1-hour overlapping array boundary, entering on the 1-minute timeframe lacks high probability.

may_differ.reason: Traidle requires specific displacement for FVGs; the presenter combines arrays organically without strictly quantifying the displacement magnitude.

signals_observed.bias_source: 1H timeframe showing two overlapping discount arrays (FVG + small breaker).

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Identifies 1-hour context: price retraces into a 1H overlapping FVG and small breaker.
Drops to 5-minute timeframe, waits for an expansion out of the 1H zone.
Price retraces into the first 5-minute overlapping discount array (an order block and a fair value gap).
Stop loss is placed safely below the intermediate term low to account for market probability, instead of tightly under the entry array.
Price expands and hits the take profit target at the intermediate term highs.

examples.presenter_commentary: He heavily stresses not to place the stop loss too tightly (e.g., just below the entry array). He advises giving the trade room to breathe by placing the stop below the structural intermediate term low to avoid random stop-outs.

may_differ.reason: Presenter uses structural logic (intermediate term low) rather than strict pip-based or array-edge-based invalidation.
